wu: Students play 'Find the Pair' with shopping flashcards. Teacher places 10 item cards on the board. Students take turns finding two matching cards and saying 'I have a [shirt].'
wuAlt: Students play 'Shopping Bingo' with 3x3 grids of food items. Teacher calls out items, students mark them and shout 'Bingo!' when full.
Students do a quick 'Two Truths and a Lie' about their favorite shops using 'I like...' and 'I don't like...'.
pres: Teacher shows a broken toy and says 'This toy is broken. I need help.' Elicits complaint frames using flashcards: 'This [item] is [problem].' Models 'This T-shirt is too small.' Checks understanding with 'Show me a problem with a bag.'
presAlt: Teacher uses a dialogue video of a customer returning a phone. Pauses to elicit problem phrases.
Teacher writes a complaint on the board with gaps, students guess the missing words like 'This laptop is not working.'
prac: Students do 'Problem-Solution Matching' in pairs. They match 6 problem cards ('This phone doesn't charge') to solution cards ('Can I have a refund?'). Teacher monitors and models pronunciation.
pracAlt: Students play 'Dialogue Repair' in groups. They get a jumbled dialogue and reorder it to make a logical complaint conversation.
Students do 'Chain Complaints' in a circle. Each student adds one problem to the previous one: 'This phone is broken. This charger is lost.'
ls: Students listen to a shop dialogue and tick the problems they hear (e.g., 'too expensive', 'wrong color'). Teacher plays the audio twice, then checks answers as a class.
re: Students play 'Charades' with action words from the lesson (e.g., 'return', 'complain', 'refund'). One student mimes the word, others guess 'Are you returning?'
prod: Students roleplay a customer service scenario in pairs. One is a customer with a problem (e.g., 'This dress is torn'), the other is a shop assistant. They must use at least 2 complaint phrases and 1 solution phrase.
rw: Students read a short complaint message and circle the problem words. Then, they write their own 6-line complaint dialogue using frames like 'I bought this [item] yesterday. It is [problem]. Can I...?'
st: Teacher reads a short story about a man who returns a gift during Ramadan. Students discuss 'What would you do?' and close with 'Today we learned to complain about problems. Thank you, class.'
g: Teams race to write 3 problems on the board using 'This [item] is [problem].'
Students flip cards to find matching item and problem pairs.
Each student adds a problem to the previous one: 'This bag is old. This shirt is red.'
Pairs swap roles after each complaint practice.
Students find the mistake in a written complaint dialogue.
diff: Fast finishers write a second complaint with a different problem.
Support learners use a sentence frame handout with 'This [item] is [problem].' pre-filled.
hw: Write a short complaint message to a shop about a broken item.
Write your Ramadan daily routine in 8 sentences using 'I' and frequency adverbs like 'always'.
Draw 3 shopping problems and write the complaint for each.
tip: Link the language to Ramadan by discussing shopping routines during the holy month. Use realia like dates or lanterns to make complaints culturally relevant.
